 Joe Biden says cancer will limit him from promoting his upcoming memoir
 By Piper Hudspeth Blackburn 
 Updated Nov 8, 2026, 8:01 PM ET 
 PUBLISHED Nov 8, 2026, 7:35 PM ET 
 President Joe Biden delivers remarks in Washington, DC, on October 18, 2022. 
 Leah Millis/Reuters/File

 Former President Joe Biden announced Sunday that he “won’t be able to do as many conversations” about his upcoming presidential memoir due to his fight with prostate cancer .
 “Some days are better than others. It hasn’t stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down. What that means is, unfortunately, I won’t be able to do as many conversations about my book as I’d hoped. However, I’m hopeful the words on the page speak for themselves,” he wrote on social media .
 Biden’s book, titled “Promise Me, America,” is slated for release on November 17.
 “I hope you’ll read it,” he wrote on social media. “It covers my years as President. The challenges we faced, the decisions I made, and why I made them. It’s about who we are as a nation. What we stand for. And America’s role in the world.”
 Biden, who turns 84 on November 20, is the oldest living former president. The former president revealed his cancer diagnosis in May 2025, less than four months after he left the White House.
 His office said in a statement then that he appeared to have a “more aggressive” form of cancer but that it “appears to be hormone-sensitive which allows for effective management.”
 The former president’s son, Hunter Biden, told the BBC in August that his father’s cancer had “metastasized into his bones and further.”
 “It’s really sad to watch,” Hunter Biden said. “The only thing that I’d say about my dad, about his health right now, is I wish he would complain more, because it’s not good.”
